# Incident Report — mta-2024-08-15

## Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| Domain member of | lafontainebleu.org (DC: WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org) |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** |

Evidence: NBNS name registration (`nbns.name`) shows `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV` broadcast from 10.8.15.133; ARP confirms MAC `00:1c:bf:03:54:82` bound to that IP; Kerberos `CNameString` shows both the machine account `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` and user principal `plucero` authenticating from 10.8.15.133.

## Malware family
**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alert export was provided with this evidence set — only the pcap).

The observed TTPs match a phishing-delivered commodity loader/backdoor chain, most consistent with **Latrodectus-style loader behavior**:
- Fake FedEx tracking/invoice phishing page (`checkfedexexp.com`)
- ZIP containing a heavily junk-padded, obfuscated `.js` downloader (evasion via file inflation and `WScript.Sleep()` delays)
- Payload retrieved via **BITS (Microsoft BITS/7.8 User-Agent)** as a Win64 PE DLL
- Persistent HTTP beaconing to a bare-IP host on port 80 using a spoofed/malformed legacy browser User-Agent and a large base64-encoded `Cookie` header carrying encrypted check-in data

No file was reverse-engineered beyond static typing, so the specific family name should be treated as a behavioral hypothesis, not a confirmed identification.

## Delivery chain
1. `10.8.15.133` browses to `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` (t=74.7s) — Cloudflare-fronted (104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159), fake FedEx-themed invoice lure.
2. Server returns `application/octet-stream`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoice 876597035_003.zip"`.
3. ZIP contains a single file: `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (~6.99 MB, padded with commented-out legitimate library source/report text to inflate size and evade sandboxing; contains live `WScript.Sleep()` calls indicating a WScript-executed downloader).
4. ~60 seconds later (t=135.9s), the host uses **Microsoft BITS/7.8** to HEAD then GET `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — a 159,232-byte **Win64 PE DLL** mislabeled with `Content-Type: text/html`.
5. From t=196.9s onward, the host beacons repeatedly to `72.5.43.29:80` with `GET /` and `POST /` using a malformed User-Agent (`Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` — note the spurious space in "Mozilla / 5.0") and a large base64 `Cookie:` header holding encrypted data. Beaconing continues through the end of the capture (~1956s / 32 minutes), all to the same IP, never resolved via DNS (bare-IP C2, no matching A-record lookup in the capture).

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — repeated GET/POST `/` beacons with encrypted base64 `Cookie` header; no DNS lookup precedes this traffic (bare-IP C2). TCP streams 134, 142–, ongoing to end of capture.

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (A: 104.21.55.70, 172.67.170.159) — phishing/invoice lure, delivered the ZIP.
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (A: 172.67.170.159, 104.21.55.70) — referenced inside the downloaded JS (`/data-privacy?...` URL), part of the same phishing infrastructure.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — delivered the malicious ZIP.
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS download of the PE DLL payload.
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent` — found embedded as a string inside the JS downloader.

**Files / hashes**
| File | SHA256 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `Invoice 876597035_003.zip` | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | HTTP object export from stream to 104.21.55.70, `Content-Disposition` header |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` (inside ZIP) | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Extracted from the ZIP payload above |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (Win64 PE DLL, BITS payload) | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | HTTP object export, BITS GET/HEAD to 72.5.43.29 |

## Benign context (not indicators)
- `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `armmf.adobe.com` — legitimate Adobe ARM update-check traffic (including the `ProcessMAU.txt` fetch, benign despite the odd legacy IE7 UA — this is Adobe ARM's known behavior).
- All `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `*.bing.com`, `*.msedge.net`, `*.windows.com`, `*.office.com`, `*.wns.windows.com` traffic — standard Windows/Edge/Office telemetry, updates, and BITS-based Windows Update delivery (`msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com`).
- `sb.scorecardresearch.com`, `nelreports.net` — ad/analytics telemetry, unrelated.
- LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP/DCERPC (drsuapi, samr, lsarpc) traffic between 10.8.15.133/10.8.15.4 and the domain controller — normal AD domain-join/auth chatter, not lateral movement in this capture.
- SSDP `M-SEARCH` multicast traffic — Windows/Edge device discovery, benign.

## Summary
The Windows workstation **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), logged in as user **plucero** on the `lafontainebleu.org` domain, was infected after visiting a fake FedEx tracking/invoice phishing page at `quote.checkfedexexp.com`, which delivered a ZIP containing a heavily obfuscated JS downloader. That downloader used BITS to fetch a Win64 PE DLL from bare-IP host 72.5.43.29, which then began persistent HTTP beaconing (GET/POST to `/` with an encrypted `Cookie` header) back to `72.5.43.29:80` for the remainder of the capture. Attribution to a specific malware family (loader/backdoor consistent with Latrodectus-style TTPs) is behavioral only, as no IDS signature was available in the provided evidence.
